title: Retina anatomy: photoreceptors and neural layers
description: Rods, cones, bipolar and ganglion circuits; fovea, optic disc, pigment epithelium and dual blood supply.

questions.question: Where are rods and cones located in the retina?
questions.answer: Photoreceptors lie in the outer neural retina next to retinal pigment epithelium, even though incoming light first passes through more internal layers.

questions.question: What is the difference between rods and cones?
questions.answer: Rods are especially sensitive in low light; cones support high-acuity and color vision, particularly near the fovea.

questions.question: What are the photoreceptor segments?
questions.answer: Rod and cone inner/outer segments facing RPE. Function: Capture photons and start phototransduction.

questions.question: Where is the retinal pigment epithelium located?
questions.answer: Pigmented monolayer adjacent to photoreceptors and Bruch membrane. Function: Recycles visual pigment, phagocytoses shed discs and forms outer blood–retinal barrier.

questions.question: What is the function of the fovea centralis?
questions.answer: Function: Peak spatial acuity. Small central pit with closely spaced cones and displaced inner layers.
